title: Why you remember stories better than lists of facts
hook: You forget half your shopping list, but remember a whole film plot.

narration.text: Your brain is wired to remember stories, not just isolated facts.
This is called the narrative bias: we process information better when it is structured.
A good story has a beginning, a middle, and an end, with characters and conflicts.
This structure provides context, linking facts together in a meaningful way.
Each event in a story can trigger memories of previous events, reinforcing the information.
This is why teachers and presenters often use anecdotes to explain complex ideas.
When you need to remember something important, try turning it into a short story.
How do you usually try to remember new information?

description: Ever wondered why you can recall every detail of a movie but struggle with a simple to-do list? It's all about the narrative bias, a fascinating quirk of human memory. Discover how your brain prefers stories over plain facts.
topic: Why you remember stories better than lists of facts, explaining the narrative bias.
